# Correct the name of the GNI per capita indicator
gdp_row = df[df['Series Name'] == 'GNI per capita (constant 2015 USdollar)']

# Extract the relevant data
gdp_data = gdp_row.drop(columns=['Country Group', 'Country Code', 'Series Name', 'Series Code']).transpose()
gdp_data.columns = gdp_data.iloc[0]
gdp_data = gdp_data.drop(gdp_data.index[0])
gdp_data = gdp_data.reset_index()

# Rename the columns for clarity
gdp_data.columns = ['Year', 'SSA_GNI', 'LMC_GNI']

# Merge the data on the 'Year' column
merged_data = pd.merge(education_expenditure_data, gdp_data, on='Year')

# Display the first few rows of the merged data
merged_data.head()

# Drop rows with NaN values in the 'SSA_GNI' column
merged_data = merged_data.dropna(subset=['SSA_GNI'])

# Display the first few rows of the cleaned data
merged_data.head()

# Extract the LMC data for education expenditure and GNI
lmc_data = merged_data[['Year', 'LMC_Education_Expenditure', 'LMC_GNI']]

# Drop rows with NaN values in the 'LMC_Education_Expenditure' or 'LMC_GNI' columns
lmc_data = lmc_data.dropna(subset=['LMC_Education_Expenditure', 'LMC_GNI'])

# Display the first few rows of the cleaned LMC data
lmc_data.head()

import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

# Calculate the correlation coefficient
correlation = lmc_data['LMC_Education_Expenditure'].corr(lmc_data['LMC_GNI'])
correlation

# Plot the relationship
sns.scatterplot(x='LMC_Education_Expenditure', y='LMC_GNI', data=lmc_data)
plt.title('Relationship between Education Expenditure and GNI in LMC')
plt.xlabel('Education Expenditure (percentage of GNI)')
plt.ylabel('GNI per capita (constant 2015 US$)')
plt.show()
